subject: algebraically closed field
object: field in which every non-constant polynomial has a root
statement: An algebraically closed field is a field in which every non-constant polynomial with coefficients in the field has a root in the field.

subject: field of real numbers
statement: The field of real numbers is not algebraically closed.

subject: field of complex numbers
statement: The field of complex numbers is algebraically closed.

subject: polynomial x^2 + 1 over real numbers
statement: The polynomial x^2 + 1 has no real roots in the field of real numbers.

subject: every field K
object: contained in an algebraically closed field
statement: Every field K is contained in an algebraically closed field.

subject: finite field F
statement: No finite field F is algebraically closed.

subject: union of all finite fields of fixed characteristic p
statement: The union of all finite fields of a fixed characteristic p is an algebraically closed field.

subject: field F
object: irreducible polynomials of degree one only
statement: A field F is algebraically closed if and only if the only irreducible polynomials in F[x] are those of degree one.

subject: algebraically closed field F
object: every polynomial splits into linear factors
statement: In an algebraically closed field F, every polynomial of degree n >= 1 splits into linear factors.

subject: algebraically closed field F
statement: An algebraically closed field F has no proper algebraic extension.

subject: almost everywhere in measure theory
object: property that holds except on a set of measure zero
statement: Almost everywhere is a property that holds for all elements in a set except a subset of measure zero.

subject: Lebesgue measure
statement: When discussing sets of real numbers, the Lebesgue measure is usually assumed unless otherwise stated.

subject: almost everywhere
statement: The term almost everywhere is abbreviated a.e. in modern usage.

subject: older mathematical literature
statement: In older literature, p.p. stands for the equivalent French phrase presque partout.

subject: set with full measure
statement: A set with full measure is one whose complement is of measure zero.

subject: almost surely in probability theory
statement: In probability theory, almost surely refers to events with probability 1.

subject: analytic function
object: function locally represented by a convergent power series
statement: An analytic function is a function that is locally represented by a convergent power series.

subject: complex analytic function
statement: A complex analytic function is equivalent to a holomorphic function.

subject: real function
statement: A smooth real function need not be analytic.

subject: polynomials
statement: All polynomials are analytic functions.

subject: exponential function
statement: The exponential function is an analytic function.

subject: analytic geometry
object: study of geometry using a coordinate system
statement: Analytic geometry, also known as coordinate geometry or Cartesian geometry, is the study of geometry using a coordinate system.

subject: Menaechmus
statement: Menaechmus was a Greek mathematician who solved problems using a method resembling the use of coordinates.

subject: Apollonius of Perga
statement: Apollonius of Perga was a Greek mathematician who developed methods similar to analytic geometry in the Conics.

subject: Omar Khayyam
statement: Omar Khayyam was an 11th-century Persian mathematician.

subject: Omar Khayyam
object: Treatise on Demonstrations of Problems of Algebra
statement: Omar Khayyam authored the Treatise on Demonstrations of Problems of Algebra in 1070.

subject: analytic geometry
object: René Descartes and Pierre de Fermat
statement: Analytic geometry was independently invented by René Descartes and Pierre de Fermat.

subject: René Descartes
statement: René Descartes authored La Géométrie, published in 1637.

subject: La Géométrie
statement: La Géométrie was published in 1637.

subject: Descartes's La Géométrie
object: translated to Latin with commentary by van Schooten
statement: Descartes's La Géométrie was translated to Latin with commentary by van Schooten in 1649.

subject: Pierre de Fermat
object: Ad locos planos et solidos isagoge
statement: Pierre de Fermat authored Ad locos planos et solidos isagoge in manuscript form, circulating in Paris in 1637.

subject: analytic number theory
object: branch of number theory using mathematical analysis
statement: Analytic number theory is a branch of number theory that uses methods from mathematical analysis to solve problems about the integers.

subject: analytic number theory
statement: Analytic number theory began with Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet's 1837 introduction of Dirichlet L-functions.

subject: Dirichlet's theorem on arithmetic progressions
statement: Dirichlet's theorem on arithmetic progressions was published in 1837.

subject: multiplicative number theory
object: deals with distribution of prime numbers
statement: Multiplicative number theory deals with the distribution of prime numbers.

subject: additive number theory
object: concerned with additive structure of integers
statement: Additive number theory is concerned with the additive structure of the integers.

subject: prime number theorem
statement: The prime number theorem states that x/ln(x) is a good approximation to the prime-counting function π(x).

subject: Adrien-Marie Legendre
statement: Adrien-Marie Legendre conjectured in 1797 or 1798 that π(a) is approximated by a/(A ln(a) + B).

subject: Carl Friedrich Gauss
object: wrote note about prime distribution c. 1792-1793
statement: Carl Friedrich Gauss wrote a note about prime number distribution in his logarithm table around 1792 or 1793.

subject: Bernhard Riemann
object: single short paper on number theory
statement: Bernhard Riemann published a single short paper on number theory investigating the Riemann zeta function.

subject: Riemann hypothesis
statement: The Riemann hypothesis is one of Bernhard Riemann's conjectures about properties of the zeta function.

subject: prime number theorem
statement: The prime number theorem was proved independently by Jacques Hadamard and Charles de la Vallée-Poussin in 1896.

subject: Pafnuty L'vovich Chebyshev
statement: Pafnuty L'vovich Chebyshev published papers on the asymptotic law of distribution of prime numbers in 1848 and 1850.

subject: Chebyshev's work
statement: Chebyshev's estimates for π(x) were strong enough to prove Bertrand's postulate.

subject: zero of a function
object: value x where function equals zero
statement: A zero of a function f is a member x of the domain of f such that f(x) vanishes at x.

subject: root of a polynomial
object: zero of the corresponding polynomial function
statement: A root of a polynomial is a zero of the corresponding polynomial function.

subject: fundamental theorem of algebra
object: polynomial has at most degree number of roots
statement: The fundamental theorem of algebra shows that any non-zero polynomial has a number of roots at most equal to its degree.

subject: polynomial f(x) = x^2 - 5x + 6
statement: The polynomial f(x) = x^2 - 5x + 6 has the two roots 2 and 3.

subject: real odd polynomial
object: must have at least one real root
statement: Every real polynomial of odd degree must have at least one real root.

subject: real even polynomial
statement: A real polynomial of even degree may have no real roots.

subject: zero set of function f
statement: The zero set of a function is the set of all its zeros.

subject: kernel of linear map
statement: The zero set of a linear map is also known as its kernel.
